curated.instructions: omr/instructions/8845-1/ (scans of two-page spreads; the buggy is steps 1-14, pages 3-5; alternate models after, motorising photos on page 9, the suspension photo on the back cover)

functions.does: The steering wheel steers the front wheels: its column bends through a universal joint to a 16 tooth gear, which turns a second 16 tooth gear on the pinion's axle; its 8 tooth gear drives a rack on the tie bar, which swings both steering arms the same way.
functions.source: book: steps 4-8 (steering arms, tie bar and rack, pinion, column and wheel)

functions.does: Each rear wheel rides on its own trailing arm, which pivots on the cross axle ahead of it: pushed up, the arm swings up and the shock absorber between it and the frame shortens.
functions.source: book: steps 1-2 (arms and their axle) and 9 (shock absorbers); the back cover photo shows it sprung

functions.does: The shock absorbers' springs hold the rear arms down, so the buggy stands on its rear wheels and springs back when pushed down.
functions.skip: only matters under load; the arms' swing is the function above

functions.does: Pushed along, all four wheels roll freely: the front ones on axle pins in the steering arms, the rear ones on axles in the trailing arms.
The roll cage holds its shape: its toothed toggle joints grip at the angles they're set to, so the cage stands rigid over the seat.
functions.note: not a control: the cage should not move whatever is turned

why: p100 4185 has no joint to work
